newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine industrial output to slow in H2 - FIEL.
newsitem.headline: Argentine industrial output to slow in H2 - FIEL.

text.p: Argentine industry cannot sustain the industrial output growth of more than 8.0 percent seen in the first half of 1997 for the rest of the year, Abel Viglione, chief economist at FIEL consultancy, said Thursday.

"If there is no external shock, the rate of industrial production growth will be between 5.5-6.5 percent in the second half, a lower rate but not a bad one," Viglione wrote in an article published in financial daily El Cronista.

"In addition, it will be higher than the average seen during the second half of 1994," added the economist, looking at the high growth period before the recession sparked by the "Tequila Effect" devaluation of the Mexican peso of end-1994.
FIEL released preliminary figures showing industrial output was up 9.9 percent in June from the same month in 1996.
In the second quarter, production was up 8.2 percent compared with the same quarter a year earlier. In the first quarter, it rose 8.1 percent from the same period a year ago.

Viglione explained that production rises in consumer durables accounted for 38 percent of the rise in FIEL's industrial output index, while capital goods production increases explained another 30 percent of the rise.
